requirement_text: 0 high dependency advisories; 0 high DAST findings; no medium unresolved > 30 days
record_type: runtime SCA gates plus seeded OWASP ZAP full scans

sca.scope_note: The remaining picomatch advisory is confined to the dev build toolchain and remains documented; the runtime-scoped gates hide neither that advisory nor any high advisory.

dast.harness: web/scripts/run-dast.mjs (disposable PostgreSQL 17 + API + Vite stack, seeded from the E2E global setup)

sessions.source: admin.json storageState from createAdminAccount (database promotion plus TOTP enrollment and verification)
user.json storageState from createVerifiedAccount (invite, registration, destination verification and sign-in)

documented_environment_exclusions.name: HTTP Only Site
documented_environment_exclusions.reason: The DAST target is a disposable HTTP-only compose stack. TLS termination is a per-environment control recorded by the separate manual review, so this rule is not a defect of the scanned stack.

medium_review.mechanism: One GitHub issue per stable finding fingerprint records first-seen and last-seen dates; a high finding fails immediately, a medium issue older than 30 days fails the nightly job, and a finding no longer observed is closed.

verdict: PASS - 0 high runtime dependency advisories, 0 high DAST findings and 0 unexcluded medium DAST findings across seeded admin and user full scans; the 30-day issue-age review is enforced on every nightly run.
caveats: The ZAP target is an ephemeral HTTP-only compose stack; TLS remains a separate per-environment manual control, and rule 10106 is excluded with that rationale in web/zap/finding-exclusions.json.
The admin JWT is deliberately limited to 15 minutes, so the admin scan runs first; a future change that lengthens scans beyond that window must re-seed the admin session or add ZAP re-authentication.
ZAP is a point-in-time dynamic scan of crawled routes; it does not replace manual security review of flows the spider and Ajax spider cannot reach.
